arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Merrill Lynch argues the statute uses one consistent definition for all parties.
Dabit argues the definition changes based on who brings the lawsuit.
Justice Roberts noted that preemption might require a narrower reading than enforcement.
Justice Scalia asked about the SEC's enforcement authority in this specific area.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Securities Litigation Uniform Standards Act. The statute preempts certain state securities class actions. The parties disagree on how broadly to read the phrase in connection with. This phrase appears in federal securities laws. The interpretation determines which court hears these cases.

sections.heading: What each side wants

Dabit wants the Supreme Court to reverse the removal and keep the case in state court.

paragraphs: Merrill Lynch argues the phrase in connection with has one broad meaning for all plaintiffs.
Dabit argues the phrase has a narrower meaning for private investors than for regulators.
